name: Agram
description: Agram is a West African last-trick game in which only the final trick decides the hand winner.

overview.description: Agram is a West African last-trick game in which only the final trick decides the hand winner.

history.origins: Agram is one of the most popular card games in Niger. Another version is played in northern Mali (Gao, Timbuktu, Kidal) and has spread to Cameroon as Fapfap. It is related to Spar or Sipa in Ghana and West Africa, probably descended from a European game introduced during the slave trade era.
timeline: Documented in modern card-game surveys as a popular Niger game.
Related local forms such as Sink-Sink and Fapfap use similar last-trick structure.
history.cultural: Known for tactical card conservation because only the final trick matters.
history.evolution: Regional variants mostly change hand size and scoring stakes, while keeping the last-trick objective.

setup.players: Two to five players; typically two to four. With six cards each and a 35-card pack, five is the maximum.
setup.deck: 35-card pack from a standard deck with K, Q, J, all 2s, and Ace of spades removed.
setup.dealing: Deal 6 cards each in two batches of 3 (counterclockwise in common Niger form).
setup.equipment: Deck and optional score or stake tracking.

rules.objective: Win the sixth and final trick of the hand; the player who takes that last trick wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads first trick. Players must follow suit if able; otherwise they may discard any card. Highest card in led suit wins the trick and leads next. Winner of trick six wins the hand.
keyRules: Only led suit can win a trick.
Winner of final trick wins the deal.

strategy.basic: Preserve control cards for late tricks rather than spending them early.
strategy.intermediate: Track void suits to predict forced discards before final trick.
strategy.advanced: Shape trick flow so your lead/control aligns with trick six rather than intermediate trick count.
tips: Early sacrifice can be correct if it improves your final-trick position.
Count remaining high cards in each suit as tricks progress.

scoring.winCondition: Win the sixth and final trick.

synthesis.shortDescription: A no-trump trick game where winning the final trick decides the hand.
